title: CORE: stated steady ODE in (b) is not the honest reduction of (a) — operator acts on g=βf, not F

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**CORE / blocking gap — derivation of the stated steady ODE (parts (a)-(b)).**

With $p(x,y)=\varphi(y-x)$, substitute and set $r=y-x$, $g:=\beta f$:
$$2\int \beta(y)\varphi(x-y) f(y)\,dy = 2\int \varphi(-r)\,g(x+r)\,dr.$$
Taylor expanding $g(x+r)$ to second order and integrating against $\varphi$ gives the **honest** local PDE
$$\partial_t f = -(\beta+\mu)f + 2g + 2a\,\partial_x g + D\,\partial_x^2 g + O(\varepsilon^3),\qquad g=\beta f.$$
Inserting $f=e^{\lambda t}F$ yields the **variable-coefficient** ODE
$$D(\beta F)'' + 2a(\beta F)' + (\beta-\mu-\lambda)F = 0.\qquad\text{(ODE-true)}$$

But the problem's target form (part (b)) is
$$\tfrac{D}{2}F'' - aF' + (\beta-\mu-\lambda)F = 0.\qquad\text{(ODE-target)}$$

These **do not agree**: (ODE-true) has the diffusion/drift acting on the product $g=\beta F$ (with cross terms $D F\beta''$, $2DF'\beta'$, $2aF\beta'$) and coefficients $D, 2a$, whereas (ODE-target) has $\beta$ pulled outside and coefficients $D/2, a$.

**Required of any proof.** Justify (ODE-true) $\Rightarrow$ (ODE-target) explicitly. This needs: (i) a precise statement of the "appropriately rescaled local-transition regime" (e.g. diffusive scaling $a=\alpha\varepsilon,\ D=\delta\varepsilon^2$ with a rescaled $x$), (ii) a slowly-varying-$\beta$ / WKB hypothesis to move $\beta$ outside the derivatives and drop $\beta',\beta''$ cross terms, and (iii) the factor-of-2 normalization mapping $(D,2a)\to(D/2,a)$. Every approximation must be a stated hypothesis, not silent. This is definitional-drift risk (skill F1): silently treating the operator as acting on $F$ invalidates parts (c)-(e).

(Symbolically verified with sympy that (ODE-true) and (ODE-target) differ.)
